thread:
alex: Quick q — I switched my 401(k) elections from pre-tax to Roth mid-quarter because of the new vendor cutover. How does that affect employer match? Will previous pre-tax contributions still get matched, or will match be based on the payroll posting date? Need to know if I should file anything to get retro match. Thanks.
benefits-bot: Reminder: elections made in the benefits portal apply to future payrolls once processed. See https://benefits.redwood.example/enroll :calendar: 
maria: Hey @alex — short answer: match is calculated on what posts to payroll for the pay period. So contributions that were deducted pre-cutover and posted as pre-tax should still be matched as usual. If anything failed to post because of the vendor migration we can do a retro adjustment. Can you DM me a payroll date?
alex: Thanks — pay date was Oct 15 (paid 10/15). I changed elections on Oct 10 via the new portal. Not sure what actually posted.
jamal: Hi @alex @maria — payroll here. For our biweekly schedule, changes submitted and confirmed in the portal before 12:00pm PT 2 business days prior to pay date make it into that payroll. If the vendor migration caused delayed posting, we can request a retro via GL code 'RET401'. Retro adjustments must be requested within 90 days of pay date. We need the employee ID and pay period end. We're happy to process if people-ops approves.
maria: Process: 1) Alex, please fill the 'Retro Contribution Request' form at https://benefits.redwood.example/forms (link) — include pay period end & employee ID. 2) People Ops will verify. 3) Payroll will process with GL: RET401 and tag match. Sample fields:
``
employee_id: 12345
pay_period_end: 2025-10-15
contribution_type: 401k
amount_pre_tax_posted: $XXX
requested_retro_match: yes
```
I'll review once submitted.
alex: One more Q — does this impact my HSA contribution or employer HSA contribution? I also switched HSA elections same day.
maria: HSA is separate: employer HSA contributions follow our HR rules and are based on what's recorded per pay period too. If HSA deductions didn't post because of migration we can include HSA in the retro request, but HSA employer contributions have their own GL (RET-HSA) and may have different tax treatment. I'll flag it in the form.
jamal: :thumbsup: We'll process both as long as the retro forms have clear amounts. Note: catch-up contributions (50+) are treated like pre-tax if they were elected as pre-tax; if you switched to Roth catch-up, that's a plan-level thing — message me if that's the case.
alex: Got it — submitting form now. Thanks both! :pray:
maria: Thanks @alex — once you submit, I'll ack and loop payroll. Will update thread.
